chapter: Leaving Dinah Shore and his daughters
title: Leaving Dinah Shore to establish himself in Los Angeles studios
summary: On Iris's urging he quit Dinah, who begged him to stay, and she got her own show soon after.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We digressed a little bit there, going back to Cab Calloway's band and some of the relationships that you and I had together in that band, and now we should jump back up to where we were in California. Now you left Dinah Shore -- were there any particular reasons you left? Did you go to the recording studios or what? That was the next thing you did here.

I thought that while I was with her, I was doing quite a few record dates out there in California, so between my friends out there and my wife, they kept talking to me about staying in town; they said that would be the way I could get established.
This is Iris, now, your wife, Iris?

Yeah, my wife, Iris; she was telling me that would be the only way I could get established, if I keep going out all the time, you know, I mean, I could never get myself established in the recording field, so that's why I left Dinah.
And when I got ready to leave her, she almost got on her knees and begged me not to leave; she wanted to

know, she said, 'What are you leaving for?', you know, and I told her, and she said, 'What's the matter? You're not happy here with me?' -- and you know, I told her, I said, 'I'm happy' -- which I was -- but that I had to please, I thought I had to please my wife, and I also thought I was doing the right thing because I wanted to get myself established in California at a studio.

And I think that was one of the worst moves I ever made in my life, because six months after I left Dinah, she got her own show, and she's been doing that show now for almost six years, without any interruption. Yeah, I was really sorry I lost out on that.
So what did you do in California then?
